title: Assistant Professor of Economics in the College of Social Studies
description:
Wesleyan University, founded in 1831, is a diverse,
energetic liberal arts community where critical thinking and
practical idealism go hand in hand.

JEL Classifications:

B00: History of Economic Thought, Methodology, and Heterodox
Approaches: General

N00: Economic History: General

P00: Political Economy and Comparative Economic Systems:
General

Wesleyan University’s College of Social Studies invites
applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in the College
of Social Studies position beginning July 1, 2027 from scholars
with primary research and teaching interests in history of economic
thought, economic history, political economy, and/or economic
philosophy. Candidates must have a Ph.D. in economics in hand by
the time of appointment in order to be hired as an assistant
professor. However, a successful candidate could be hired initially
as an instructor if they are on track to complete the degree within
one year of hire, at which point the rank would be converted to
assistant professor. Advanced assistant professors of economics are
also encouraged to apply. The teaching load is four courses per
year. Additional duties include advising and mentoring students,
carrying on a sustained and professionally visible program of
research, and participating in faculty governance at the college
and university levels. The College of Social Studies (CSS) is a
rigorous, multidisciplinary major focusing on history, government,
and social theory in addition to economics. Founded in 1959, the
CSS is reading and writing intensive, encouraging intellectual
independence with weekly essays, small group tutorials, and a
vibrant intellectual community . Wesleyan values both scholarship
and teaching very highly, has a strong, diverse undergraduate
student body, and offers a generous sabbatical program and
competitive salaries and benefits.

Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching
evaluations if available, and a sample of scholarly writing via the
online application portal. In the cover letter, applicants should
describe how they support the college's commitment to fostering an
inclusive community. You will also be asked to provide the email
addresses of three referees from whom we will obtain confidential
letters of recommendation. Complete applications must be received
by November 15, 2026, to be assured of full consideration. Contact
Martha Crebbin with questions at mcrebbin@wesleyan.edu.

The salary range for this position is between $93,500 and
$98,500.

Work Location: On Campus

All offers to external applicants are contingent on the candidate’s
completion of a 
pre-employment background check screening to the satisfaction
of Wesleyan University.
